hero.title: Aurora Platform
hero.tagline: Infrastructure orchestration following the controlplane / dataplane / agent model — providing authn/authz, IAM, topology, billing, and task pipelines for tenants running on heterogeneous runtimes.
hero.goal: Goal: cleanly separate orchestration authority from workload execution, keep the source of truth in PostgreSQL, and use Redis as the safe realtime coordination channel for HA.

planes.section_desc: Aurora cleanly separates three layers of responsibility — no layer overlaps another.

controlplane.title: Controlplane
controlplane.desc: Central orchestration layer — accepts requests, validates policy, writes canonical state to DB, dispatches commands to dataplane/agent.

dataplane.title: Dataplane
dataplane.desc: Runtime layer near resources — consumes commands, executes tasks, reports state back to controlplane.

agent.title: Agent
agent.desc: Edge process near host/node/VM — receives specific commands, performs local side-effects, sends heartbeat & result.

architecture.title: System Architecture
architecture.desc: Data flow between client, edge proxy, controlplane cluster, dataplane workers, agents, and infrastructure stores.
architecture.footer: PostgreSQL is source of truth · Redis is the realtime coordination channel · Envoy is the only client-facing edge

request_flow.title: Main request flow
request_flow.desc: Each HTTP/gRPC request goes through fixed layers to ensure policy & audit.
request_flow.s1_desc: Admin UI, Cloud UI, API client calls HTTP/gRPC
request_flow.s2_desc: TLS termination, vhost routing, mTLS between cluster
request_flow.s3_desc: request ID → auth → access log → rate limit → origin/cookie guard
request_flow.s5_desc: Business logic + policy decision, call repository if DB needed
request_flow.s6_desc: Only place that emits SQL to PostgreSQL
request_flow.s7_desc: Service writes state then enqueues job/event to Redis Stream
request_flow.s8_desc: Handler returns — no internal error leakage to client

modules.title: Business modules
modules.desc_prefix: Controlplane is split by business module under

principles.title: Design principles
principles.desc: Architectural constraints that keep the codebase healthy as it scales.
principles.p1_desc: Handler → Service → Repository → DB. No skipping, no mixing. SQL only in repository.
principles.p2_desc: All durable business state lives in PostgreSQL. Redis is for queue/cache/coordination/transient state only.
principles.p3_desc: Each module owns its errorx. No internal error leaks to client; handler maps to standard HTTP codes.
principles.p4_desc: Never store raw secret/token/key in DB. Plaintext only exists transiently in RAM.
principles.p5_desc: Transient Redis loss does not corrupt state. PostgreSQL is the canonical replay/reconcile source.
principles.p6_desc: Authentication errors must be generic — never leak whether a user exists or not.
